topic: Knowledge distillation and model compression for edge deployment
final_review:
Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as crucial techniques for edge deployment of deep neural networks (DNNs) due to their ability to reduce computational complexity and memory requirements (Gou et al., 2021). Model compression techniques aim to reduce the size of DNNs while maintaining their accuracy, whereas knowledge distillation focuses on transferring knowledge from a complex teacher model to a simpler student model (Cheng et al., 2017). Knowledge distillation has been widely adopted in various applications, including object detection (Chen et al., 2017). The technique involves training a student model to mimic the behavior of a teacher model, resulting in a more compact and efficient student model. Self-distillation, a variant of knowledge distillation, has been proposed to further improve the efficiency of neural networks (Zhang et al., 2021). By training a student model to mimic its own predictions, self-distillation can lead to more compact and accurate models. Model compression techniques, on the other hand, aim to reduce the size of DNNs by pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation (Cheng et al., 2017). Pruning involves removing redundant connections in the network, while quantization reduces the precision of model weights and activations. Knowledge distillation can be used in conjunction with these techniques to further improve model compression. For instance, knowledge distillation can be used to transfer knowledge from a complex teacher model to a pruned student model (Gou et al., 2021). Recent studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of knowledge distillation in model compression for edge deployment. Another study on CNN model compression used knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge from a complex teacher model to a simpler student model, resulting in a more compact and efficient model (Wang et al., 2022). However, there are still some research gaps and contradictions in the existing literature. For instance, some studies have reported conflicting results on the effectiveness of knowledge distillation in model compression (Ghojogh et al., 2026). Additionally, there is a need for more studies on the application of knowledge distillation in real-world edge deployment scenarios. In conclusion, knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for edge deployment of DNNs. While knowledge distillation has been widely adopted in various applications, there is still a need for more research on its effectiveness in model compression and edge deployment. References:
